transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Senthil (Redwood SE), Marcus Hale (Hydrangea CTO), Laila Ortiz (Hydrangea Head of Security), Nina Park (Hydrangea Platform Engineering), Alex Chen (Hydrangea Procurement)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
Hydrangea is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing inference pipelines. Primary concerns: SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML integration with Okta, RBAC for multi-team access, audit log retention and format, encryption/KMS model (BYOK vs Redwood-managed), and data residency/retention policy. They want a decision framework to pick between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem) options. Next: exchange docs, run latency baseline, schedule pilot deep-dive.

Topics covered:
- Compliance artifacts (SOC 2, ISO)
- Identity integration (SAML/Okta, SCIM)
- RBAC and token scoping for teams
- Audit logs: format, retention, exportability
- Encryption and KMS: BYOK, HSM options, e2e encryption discussion
- Data retention policies and purge workflows
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and TCO

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Marcus: Good, thanks. Marcus here. Busy week but excited to dig in.
[00:09] Laila: Hi, Laila. I'm mostly here for the security chat—want to make sure we cover audit and KMS bits.
[00:13] Nina: Nina — I'll follow up on infra specifics and traffic patterns.
[00:15] Alex: Alex from procurement, quick intro — just here to understand timeline and gating items.
[00:18] Priya: Great. We'll try to cover both high-level and get into detail. quick agenda: compliance artifacts, identity, RBAC, logs, encryption, and deployment options.
[00:28] Jordan: First, can you tell us a bit about your primary constraints? retention windows, regulators, that sort of thing.
[00:33] Marcus: Sure. We're building a chat assistant that will surface customer billing and support info. So data includes PII and billing tokens. We have to meet SOC2 and we're evaluating ISO27001. We prefer keeping customer data in us-east and eu-west for residency. Retention-wise: most PII needs to be deletable within 30 days on request, but we have logs we'd like to keep for 365 days for fraud analysis.
[00:54] Laila: Also, we have a hard requirement that keys for production models be customer-managed where possible. We want BYOK/HSM integration for the highest tier.
[01:02] Jordan: Understood. Redwood supports BYOK via KMS integration — we have docs for AWS KMS, GCP KMS and Azure Key Vault; we also offer HSM integrations for Private deployments. For Hosted we can support customer KMS with envelope encryption patterns, though we can talk through tradeoffs.
[01:18] Priya: To add, for Dedicated we can provide stronger isolation and allow you to bring keys into a more tightly managed flow. For Private on-prem — full control, but higher ops cost.
[01:29] Marcus: Can you explain the envelope thing quickly? sometimes the engineering team gets lost in the jargon.
[01:33] Priya: Sure. Briefly: payloads are encrypted client-side or at ingress with your KMS wrapping key; Redwood's runtime sees only decrypted tokens if you choose to let us manage key access, or we can perform decryption in a customer-controlled enclave when deployed Private. The envelope key pattern lets you rotate keys without re-encrypting huge datasets.
[01:50] Laila: And auditability—what logs do you provide? we need to show model inputs were handled, redactions, access events, admin actions.
[01:58] Jordan: We stream structured audit logs with request id, model id, redwood-user (or token id), timestamp, bytes in/out, and action types. We can also tag logs with customer-provided metadata. Retention is configurable; default is 90 days for hosted. We can extend to 365 under enterprise agreements.
[02:15] Nina: Format? JSON lines? and is there an export API or S3 integration?
[02:19] Priya: JSONL by default. We push to your S3 or GCS bucket, or you can pull via API. For Dedicated we support longer retention in the cluster and direct access to logs in-place.
[02:32] Marcus: For compliance audit we need immutable logs — append-only, tamper-evident. How do you handle that?
[02:39] Jordan: We integrate with object-store versioning + signed manifests to make tampering difficult. For Private we can offer write-once storage patterns or integrate with your audit trail HSM. We'll share the SOC 2 artifact that explains our controls.
[02:52] Laila: Speaking of SOC 2, do you have latest report? and ISO?
[02:55] Jordan: Yes, we have a SOC 2 Type II from 2026 and an ISO 27001 certificate — I'll send the redacted reports after today's call. There are some shared items we redact for customer privacy, but the auditor contact and scope are listed.
[03:09] Alex: On timeline: procurement wants to know what needs to be on the SOW to get Dedicated or Private. Any red flags that elongate the procurement cycle?
[03:18] Jordan: The Private/on-prem path typically requires an architecture review and a security questionnaire; Dedicated is simpler but still requires a standard security review and an MSS for KMS if BYOK. We'll provide a checklist.
[03:29] Nina: What's the typical lead time to stand up Dedicated GPU pools?
[03:32] Priya: From contract to first capacity usually 4–6 weeks if we have standard quotas; if you need specific GPUs or on-prem rack space it can be longer. For pilots we often start with Hosted plus a dedicated tenant to validate workload.
[03:46] Marcus: We're sensitive about latency for the realtime portions. Can you speak to latency SLOs and how routing works?
[03:53] Priya: We have latency SLOs depending on model family and instance selection. For Hosted we route to nearest region; Dedicated reduces multi-tenant jitter; Private gives you control over network hops. We can run a baseline test with your sample prompts to quantify.
[04:08] Jordan: We'll note that as an action item — run a baseline with your 95th-percentile prompt.
[04:12] Nina: We'll provide traffic shape and a few 95p examples.
[04:15] Laila: On RBAC: we need scoping by team and by function—some folks should be able to call embeddings only, others full generate. Also admin consoles should be restricted. How granular is your RBAC?
[04:27] Priya: We support role-based scopes: read-only, generate, admin, billing. For tokens you can create scoped API keys per environment, and for SSO we integrate with SAML + SCIM for group sync. Token-level scoping is possible so you can limit endpoints. There's also route-level allowlists for models.
[04:44] Marcus: Do you support session-based ephemeral tokens for client-side use?
[04:48] Priya: Yes, you can issue short-lived tokens via our control plane that exchange backends when embedded in client apps — it's common for mobile web flows.
[04:55] Alex: Procurement question — if we want BYOK and extended retention, is pricing significantly higher?
[05:01] Jordan: Extended retention and BYOK for Hosted are typically add-ons; Dedicated bundles retention and isolation into the seat price. We'll share a TCO comparison in the spreadsheet.
[05:10] Laila: Data residency — we must ensure that EU user data never traverses outside eu-west region. Does Redwood provide region pinning?
[05:17] Priya: Yes region pinning is supported for Hosted requests via routing policies; Dedicated and Private are naturally region-isolated. We can also set fallback policies to prevent cross-region failovers if that violates your residency rules.
[05:29] Marcus: A corner case — model updates. If Redwood rolls a new model or patch, how do you handle compatibility and can we pin versions?
[05:36] Jordan: You can pin model versions per endpoint. Automatic rollouts are opt-in; we recommend canaries for production traffic. We'll also surface regression alerts if a model drift is detected.
[05:47] Nina: For audits, we need historical model versions tied to requests so we can show what model produced an output on a given day. Do logs include model version?
[05:55] Priya: Yes, logs include model id and version hash. We also store inference config used at the time so you can reproduce results.
[06:03] Laila: About deletion — when a user requests data deletion, how quickly do you purge model KV caches and logs? Does deletion propagate to backups?
[06:12] Jordan: For Hosted, we have deletion flows that remove user-level traces from primary storage and mark logs for redaction; full scrub from backups may be eventually consistent and depends on retention policy — we can shorten backup retention in Dedicated/Private. For strict GDPR use cases we recommend Private or Dedicated with tailored retention windows.
[06:31] Marcus: If we go Private, who performs security patching?
[06:35] Priya: If it's on-prem managed by Hydrangea, you'll own patching; if you take Redwood-managed Private (we provide a managed appliance), we will handle patching under the SLA. We can detail responsibilities in the runbook.
[06:47] Alex: Any standard SOC2 exceptions or open items we should flag to legal?
[06:51] Jordan: There are a few third-party integrations with subservice orgs — we list them. We'll provide a vendor map and the SOC2 scope that highlights in-scope services. Also any customer-specific encryption needs will be spelled out.
[07:05] Nina: For SAML/Okta: do you support SCIM group sync?
[07:09] Priya: Yes SCIM v2 supported. We map groups to RBAC roles so provisioning is automated. We'll share the SAML metadata + SCIM endpoints as part of the integration guide.
[07:20] Marcus: For the model infra: do you expose any internal metrics for observability? We'd like to push to Prometheus and have traces tied to request ids.
[07:29] Priya: We surface request-level traces and integrate with OTLP/Jaeger. For Dedicated/Private we can provide Prometheus exporters. For Hosted we expose metrics via the console and you can pull logs into your SIEM.
[07:40] Laila: Is there a way to redact PII before it hits the model runtime?
[07:44] Priya: You can do client-side redaction or use Redwood's preprocessor rules to mask sensitive fields. We also have a callback pattern to let you intercept a request for inline redaction. Note: redact patterns can affect model accuracy so we advise testing.
[07:58] Marcus: Any limits on the size of logs or events we can export?
[08:02] Jordan: Throughput limits depend on plan — we'll surface quotas. Typically logs are batched and shipped; Dedicated gets higher throughput.
[08:10] Alex: Procurement note — can we get a clean copy of your DPA and standard MSS?
[08:14] Jordan: Yes, we'll attach the DPA + MSS to the docs packet.
[08:18] Priya: Quick technical note: when we talk about KMS integration for Hosted, the lingering nuance is whether you want the runtime to perform decryption or whether we perform envelope decryption only on ephemeral workers that don't persist keys. It's a control plane vs data-plane split.
[08:33] Nina: That matters. We'd prefer ephemeral decryption in an enclave so keys never live on disk. Is that available?
[08:38] Priya: For Private we can run in an enclave or on your hardware. For Hosted we have ephemeral workers and can do ephemeral KMS calls but it depends on the threat model — we'll capture both designs.
[08:49] Marcus: What about model fine-tuning or private models? If we host our own models in Redwood, how is access controlled?
[08:56] Priya: We support private model uploads; access is controlled via RBAC and tenancy. For Dedicated/Private you get full model repo control. We also support model signing to ensure integrity.
[09:08] Laila: Regarding audit export — will exported logs include full request payloads? We're sensitive about storing PII in audit.
[09:15] Jordan: You can choose full payloads, partial (redacted), or metadata-only. We can also provide PII tags in logs so your SIEM can decide retention.
[09:27] Marcus: That sounds good. Are there any limitations on encryption-at-rest for embeddings? Some vendors don't encrypt derived embeddings.
[09:34] Priya: We encrypt embeddings at-rest — with keys in KMS; you can opt for envelope encryption with BYOK.
[09:41] Alex: Procurement curiosity — have you done FedRAMP or other high-reg regimes?
[09:44] Jordan: We haven't achieved FedRAMP yet. For government or extremely regulated verticals we recommend Private/on-prem and can work a path.
[09:54] Nina: For pilot scoping — we want to run 10k requests/day and 95p latency under 300ms for short prompts. Is that realistic on Hosted?
[10:03] Priya: Depends on model and token counts. For small models and optimized kernels yes; for longer context or large models it's trickier. We'll baseline.
[10:11] Jordan: We'll capture the 95p test as part of the baseline.
[10:14] Laila: Crossover risk question — if a Redwood engineer needs to debug our tenant on Hosted, do they get access to cleartext data?
[10:22] Priya: Access is tightly controlled. We require customer approval and use ephemeral session logs; engineers access sanitized debug views and use time-limited access tokens with session recording. All actions are audited.
[10:34] Marcus: Any SLA credits for security incidents tied to log retention failures?
[10:38] Jordan: SLA terms for security incidents are in the enterprise contract — we'll include MTTD/MTTR commitments and credits for measurable downtime or breach of SLA. Security incident handling playbook is part of the artifact packet.
[10:51] Alex: Can you give a rough compare: Hosted (with BYOK + retention add-ons) vs Dedicated vs Private in one sentence each?
[10:58] Jordan: Hosted = fastest to prod, lower ops, add-on controls for keys and retention but limited by multi-tenant policies. Dedicated = reserved capacity and stronger isolation with enterprise retention and KMS controls. Private = maximum control and residency but highest ops and lead time.
[11:13] Priya: I'll add — Dedicated is where many customers land: good compromise of control and speed.
[11:18] Marcus: Ok, let's talk timeline. We want a pilot in August, procurement signoff in September. Is that feasible?
[11:25] Jordan: Yes, if we start the baseline this week and exchange docs, pilot in August is feasible. We'll need the SSO and traffic samples to scope.
[11:34] Laila: We'll also send the security questionnaire — expect some follow-ups.
[11:38] Jordan: Perfect. We'll also include our suggested risk mitigations for data residency and BYOK.
[11:44] Priya: Technical note for follow-up: I'll propose a test harness that runs 1k synthetic requests with your 95p prompts and measures tail latency and token cost.
[11:55] Nina: We'll provide the samples and a small sandbox account if needed.
[11:58] Jordan: Great. Any other blockers?
[12:00] Marcus: Not right now. Laila might have a few follow-ups post-call.
[12:03] Laila: Minor: want to confirm log signature format for auditor ingestion — we'll attach a sample schema.
[12:08] Jordan: Noted. We'll surface the log schema in the doc pack.
[12:12] Alex: From procurement — pricing tiers and MSS please.
[12:15] Jordan: Will send.
[12:18] Priya: One more question — do you have any existing encryption policies that would block keys from being shared with third parties?
[12:24] Laila: Yes, by default keys must be customer-owned for production. We might accept Redwood-managed keys in a non-prod environment.
[12:33] Jordan: That's fine; we'll architect the pilot to use customer-managed KMS and then evaluate ops tradeoffs.
[12:40] Marcus: Ok, let's recap quick and confirm next steps.
[12:44] Jordan: Recap: Jordan to send SOC2/ISO artifacts, DPA, MSS, pricing/TCO spreadsheet; Priya to run latency baseline and propose test harness; Nina to provide traffic samples and retention buckets; Laila/Marcus to confirm auditors and risk criteria. We'll schedule a technical deep-dive for the week of Jul 26 to scope Private/Dedicated specifics.
[13:09] Alex: Thanks, everyone.
[13:11] Laila: Thanks.
[13:12] Priya: Thank you — we'll follow up with the doc pack and calendar invite.
[13:16] Jordan: Thanks all, talk soon.
